sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: Repair applicability without changing the preserved ship-owned frameProfileType, structural-member/load-case ownership, canonical kN unit, cardinalities, or tolerance direction. The current StructuralMemberShape is applied to every nltl:hasStructuralMember value and requires longitudinalFrameOrientation=true and structuralLocation=sideStructureLocation, thereby incorrectly making all represented structural members applicable. Make the requirement conditional: validate the demand-versus-strength comparison only for structural-member nodes that already have the declared applicability inputs (orientation true and sideStructureLocation), while allowing non-longitudinal or non-side members and allowing no represented applicable member. Do not replace this with a convenience applicability boolean or relocate the paths.

sheets.name: ITERATIONS
rows:
Deterministic validation prevents acceptance. Fix: COMPLETE dependency relationship(s) absent from candidate: frameProfileType
Semantic validator feedback: Add the COMPLETE dependency relationship nltl:frameProfileType on the supplied ship owner, using its canonical range/value structure; it is required by the dependency contract and is currently absent. Do not relocate it to a structural member or benchmarkEntity. Preserve the existing structural-member/load-case ownership and applicability paths.

Replace qudt:KiloN with the canonical unit IRI qudt vocabulary unit http://qudt.org/vocab/unit/KiloN (the current qudt prefix resolves to http://qudt.org/schema/qudt/KiloN). Also revise the comparison semantics: midspanPlasticCollapseLoad defines plasticStrength; do not model it as an independent alternative cap unless the verified comparison model explicitly requires both thresholds. Preserve the required ship-owned frameProfileType relationship and the existing structural-member/load-case ownership paths.

Preserve the already-correct ship-owned nltl:frameProfileType relationship, structural-member/load-case ownership, and canonical unit IRI. Repair the quantity semantics: the current SPARQL only proves that at least one decimal/kN value exists and only checks distinct quantity nodes, so extra numericValue or unit values, invalid values, and multiple demand values can pass accidentally. Constrain plasticStrength, midspanPlasticCollapseLoad, and each combinedShearAndBendingDemand quantity to exactly one xsd:decimal qudt:numericValue and exactly one unit:KiloN, and ensure the comparison evaluates that single value. Also scale the equality tolerance against the expected defining value (?mv, the midspanPlasticCollapseLoad), not the reported plasticStrength (?pv), i.e. use a tolerance based on ABS(?mv).

Repair applicability without changing the preserved ship-owned frameProfileType, structural-member/load-case ownership, canonical kN unit, cardinalities, or tolerance direction. The current StructuralMemberShape is applied to every nltl:hasStructuralMember value and requires longitudinalFrameOrientation=true and structuralLocation=sideStructureLocation, thereby incorrectly making all represented structural members applicable. Make the requirement conditional: validate the demand-versus-strength comparison only for structural-member nodes that already have the declared applicability inputs (orientation true and sideStructureLocation), while allowing non-longitudinal or non-side members and allowing no represented applicable member. Do not replace this with a convenience applicability boolean or relocate the paths.
